subject: HarborAI deployment SLO debrief and next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@harborai.com>, procurement@harborai.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: HarborAI deployment SLO debrief and next steps

Hi Lena / Harbor team —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our technical deep-dive so we have shared alignment and clear next steps. I kept this intentionally short; Marissa added a technical appendix below.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Tail latency spikes during peak inference (chat bursts) impacting SLAs for live support assistants.
- Predictable per‑request cost for high-throughput inference (billing surprises right now).
- Data isolation and auditability for person‑identifiable logs (legal/regulatory).

Goals we agreed on:
1) Achieve a p95 token latency under ~200ms for median prompt length (~150 tokens) at steady state.
2) Support burst throughput up to 180 qps with graceful degradation to a lower‑cost model variant.
3) Maintain audit logs + KMS integration for request encryption and retention for 90 days.

Technical constraints and preferences you mentioned:
- Preferred model family: open‑weights (13B–34B) that retain semantic quality for concise responses (illustrative: Llama2-13B or Mistral small-medium).
- 8k context window required for some multi-turn workflows.
- Cloud VPC connectivity required; on-prem considered for regulated workloads later.

Preliminary recommendations (high level):
- Deploy on a Dedicated pool with autoscaling burst policy; reserve baseline capacity for 100 qps and enable burst to 220 qps for peak minutes.
- Use quantized 4-bit runtime builds with KV cache and prefix caching for commonly repeated prompts (saves ~30–45% token cost).
- p95 latency targets: short prompts (<=256 tokens) aim for <200ms; longer sequences will use model-tailored routing (fallback to smaller model under heavy load).

Next steps (mutual action items):
- Redwood: share SLO/cost matrix and topology sketch (attached). Owner: Sean. ETA: Tue 12/15.
- HarborAI: complete security questionnaire and confirm preferred procurement contact. Owner: Lena / procurement@harborai.com. ETA: Thu 12/17.
- Redwood SE team: propose an initial PoC plan (4 weeks) with acceptance criteria and test prompts. Owner: Marissa. ETA: Wed 12/16.

Attachments included: harborai-slo-matrix.xlsx (cost/SLO tradeoffs), harborai-topology-diagram.png (deployment options), harborai-terms-summary.pdf (billing/credits sketch).

If that matches your understanding, reply with approval and any adjustments to the schedule. I’ll queue the PoC proposal once we have procurement contact.

Best,
Sean

Thanks Sean —

This is excellent and matches our notes. A couple of clarifications:
- The 180 qps burst target is correct for our West coast peak; however, we expect sustained daytime 120 qps across multiple channels. Can you include a cost estimate for sustained 120 qps vs the 100 qps baseline?
- For latency, p95 <200ms is the right target for short prompts. For multi‑turn threads with 2–3k tokens we accept p95 <=700ms if the accuracy stays within our eval thresholds.
- Security questionnaire: we started it and pushed internal approvals to legal. Procurement (procurement@harborai.com) will coordinate with your contracts team for a standard SaaS/enterprise T&C redline.

We’re aligned on a 4-week PoC but want a short pricing guardrail before committing to reserved capacity. Can Marissa include a sample cost/throughput table for the quantized model + expected token cost with caching enabled?

I’ll confirm procurement lead and loop in Carlos for compliance answers.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Lena

Subject: Re: HarborAI deployment SLO debrief and next steps — technical appendix

Hi Lena —

Adding a slightly more technical appendix so your infra and SRE teams can see the tradeoffs and config we'd propose for the PoC. Sean outlined the non‑technical items well above.

1) Target SLOs (PoC phase):
   - p50 / p95 / p99 latency targets (short prompts <=256 tokens): 35ms / 180ms / 350ms
   - Throughput: baseline 120 qps sustained; peak bursts 220 qps (10m buckets)

2) Model and runtime recommendations:
   - Model family: Llama2-13B (4-bit quant) or Mistral 7B quantized depending on eval quality.
   - Context: 8k context support required; size of KV cache ~growth linear with concurrent sessions (we estimate ~1.2GB per 1k active sessions for 8k KV entries).

3) Deployment topology options (attached diagram):
   - Option A (Recommended for PoC): Redwood Dedicated pool in HarborAI VPC peering. Baseline nodes sized for 120 qps with autoscaling to burst. Benefits: predictable latency, easier auditing.
   - Option B (Hosted with private tenancy): Redwood-hosted endpoints with IP allowlist and customer-managed VPC tunnels. Lower ops overhead; slightly higher tail-latency variance during bursts.
   - Option C (On‑prem connector): For later compliance needs; requires node provisioning and a 2–3 week ops ramp.

4) Caching and batching approach:
   - Use prefix caching for standard system prompts and conversational templates (expected 20–25% token savings).
   - Continuous micro-batching for GPU utilization; cap batch windows to 8–12ms to avoid added tail latency.

5) Observability / acceptance criteria for PoC:
   - Real-time p95 latency dashboards per route; token-level cost breakdown; end-to-end trace for 99% of sampled requests.
   - Acceptance: p95 <=200ms for short prompts over a 48h window and 24h with sustained 120 qps.

6) Sample cost guardrail (very rough):
   - Sustained 120 qps, quantized 13B + caching: expected incremental inference cost ~$8–12k/week (depends on prompt length distribution).
   - Peak burst reservations (reserved units to limit spot price exposure): additional ~2–3k/week if reserved vs fully on‑demand.

I attached a simple SLO matrix and a topology PNG with node counts for the PoC. If you share a 48h sample of traffic shape (tokens per request distribution) we’ll refine the numbers to within 10%.

Happy to hop on a short call with your SRE/infra folks; Karthik can lead on kernel/runtime questions if you want to dig into quantization behavior.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
